answer: Each new agent identity must lock a stake before trading, and its reputation grows only when established agents verify its work. If a nebula of accounts repeats a fable of fake agreement, random audits compare outputs and slash the stake when collusion is exposed; endorsers lose reputation too. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity upfront and spend time rebuilding trust, so an attacker moving as fast as a falcon still faces real capital and opportunity costs.
